To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the DWBA calculations reproduce the main features, but not all the details, of the (p, d) cross section and analyzing power data, and the (p,d), (p,t) and (p,p) cross sections and analyzing powers can all be explained in terms of a proton optical model potential that gives strong oscillations in (p,p) and (p,t) analyzing powers, but not in (p,d) analyzing powers.

the (p,d), (p,p), and (p,2p) reaction cross sections and analyzing powers are well described by DWBA calculations when the optical model potential is constrained by the (p,p), (p,2n), and (n,2n) data.

the cross sections and analyzing powers of the (p, d) reaction on 13C and 12C and 28Si are measured and are well described by a DWBA calculation using a proton potential which reproduces the analyzing powers of (p,p) scattering.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the nuclear interior using the (p,d).
the study of nuclear structure and nuclear reactions.
the study of the structure of nuclei and the properties of nuclear forces.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the data are in accord with DWBA calculations using a proton-nucleus interaction of the same type as is used in the elastic (p,p) reaction.
the (p,p), (d,d) and (p,d) reactions are in agreement, and that the (p,d), (d,d), and (p,p) reactions are in disagreement with the (p,p') reaction.
, although the data do not prove that the (p,d), (p,n) and (d,n) data are all consistent with a single set of optical potentials, the present results are in agreement with this possibility.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the (p,p), (p,n), and (p,d) reactions at 500 MeV provide a consistent and complete description of the nuclear structure of the nuclei involved.
the data are consistent with the DWBA, but that the (p,d)- (p,p) discrepancy remains.
the (p,d), (d,p) and (p,p) reactions are consistent with a single potential.
The main takeaway from our work is that
DWBA calculations with the same potentials used in the elastic scattering can be used to extract information on the nuclear interior.
the DWBA can describe the (p,d), (p,t) and (p,3He) data at this energy, when the same proton potential is used in all three cases.
the (p,d), (p,t) and (p,3 He) reactions are all consistent with a simple picture of a direct reaction on a single proton.
